articles.title: I ran a signed PDF through 5 compressors. Two of them deleted the signature
articles.excerpt: I ran one signed PDF through five compressors. Every single output failed signature validation. The part that bothers me most is not the broken signatures. It is the two tools that deleted the signatu…
articles.body: I ran one signed PDF through five compressors. Every single output failed signature validation. The part that bothers me most is not the broken signatures. It is the two tools that deleted the signature outright, because those files look perfectly normal afterwards. The test file I didn't want to use a real contract, so I built a fake one: a one-page agreement that literally says "fictional, for testing only", with a 1800×1200 synthetic image on it. I made a throwaway root CA and a fictional signer with openssl, then signed the file with pyHanko. The signed file is 931,980 bytes. To check signatures I used two validators, poppler's pdfsig and pyHanko's own validation, both configured to trust only my test root.
articles.author: NullPointerZen

articles.body: This article contains affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. As an Amazon Associate we earn from qualifying purchases. On October 8, 2026, Omdia dropped a number that reframes the monitor market: 6.1 million OLED monitor panels will ship in 2026, up 79% from 2025 , with 7.5 million forecast for 2027. TrendForce’s Q2 data tells the same story from another angle – OLED monitor shipments nearly doubled year over year in Q2 2026 (+98%), driven largely by new 27-inch models. Meanwhile the total monitor market sits at roughly 125-130 million units a year. OLED is still a single-digit slice of that pie. It is just the slice growing fastest, and 2026 is the year the wave became undeniable. But shipment forecasts are not a buying guide.

articles.title: pdfsig said my edited signed PDF was still valid, so I compare ByteRange with the file size
articles.excerpt: I appended one line of text to the page content of a signed PDF, then ran pdfsig on it. It printed "Signature is Valid". pyHanko looked at the same file and called it an illegal modification. Both are…
articles.body: I appended one line of text to the page content of a signed PDF, then ran pdfsig on it. It printed "Signature is Valid". pyHanko looked at the same file and called it an illegal modification. Both are right about different things, and that gap is why I ended up writing a small check that compares a signature's ByteRange with the file size. Some context. Our upload service compresses PDFs before storing them, and the business side recently started sending signed contracts through it. Before letting compression touch those, I wanted two answers from code: does this file carry a signature, and has anything happened to the file since it was signed.
articles.author: hao jia

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle . What I Built Listing Lab is a private marketplace copywriter for independent Etsy, eBay, and Facebook Marketplace sellers. A seller enters the real facts about a product, chooses a marketplace and tone, and gets a title, description, highlights, and search tags. The person I built it for is the small seller who wants stronger copy but cannot justify another subscription—or uploading client and product research to an opaque service. The business case is intentionally small: charge once for a polished local tool, or bundle it with a seller workflow, without inheriting a per-generation API bill.

articles.excerpt: Stephen King's novels have inspired many movies. One of the best is also one he deeply dislikes.
articles.body: Stephen King is a vocal guy. The Master of Horror has published over 65 novels and novellas, countless short stories, and five nonfiction books since the mid-’70s. The hype that surrounds him is well deserved. King is the kind of writer who appeals to everyone, whether you’re a genre enthusiast or a literary snob. His work has been adapted into TV shows and films, and he’s never afraid to voice his complaints and praise in equal measure. But there’s one adaptational grudge that towers above all.

articles.title: 60 Years Ago, the Best Charlie Brown Quote Was So Perfect It Made It Into the Movie
articles.excerpt: Charlie Brown's bleak outlook on life was perfectly summed up in this 1966 Peanuts comic strip by Charles Schulz
articles.body: Lucy’s quote, “Happiness is a warm puppy,” is another great one that touches on life’s simple joys on a really deep level. But to determine the best quote ever uttered by Charlie Brown, I didn't want accidental brilliance, I wanted something that he understands as much as the audience does. Something where he’s telling you who he is with complete self awareness. I wanted the character's philosophy on life. To me, that’s the difference between a brilliant Charlie Brown quote and brilliant Charles Schulz quote, if that makes sense.

articles.title: GTA: San Andreas’ Bigfoot myth is a classic urban legend
articles.excerpt: The myth of the Bigfoot in GTA San Andreas might have been debunked, but it will live forever as the symbol of an exciting time in gaming.
articles.body: There is a Bigfoot in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — at least, that's what I and many others believed. Some time after the game had been released, the rumour about the new Rockstar game featuring the legendary creature spread across the internet. I remember learning about this "secret monster" from an older guy. Then I told some boys from my classroom the cool rumor I had heard about in that game our parents didn't want us to play. Word of mouth and low-resolution images shared through dial-up internet connections made GTA: San Andreas an exciting mystery.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 232 — The Lunar Dump
articles.excerpt: On Episode 232 of This Week In Space, Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Chelsea Gohd to talk about the recent large data dump from the Artemis II mission.
articles.body: On Episode 232 of This Week In Space , Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Chelsea Gohd, former writer for NASA/JPL and now with Space.com, to talk about the recent large data dump from the Artemis II mission. What was included? Why is this new data important? What observations were made, and what discoveries might result from them? What kind of annotations and notes did the astronauts include that make these observations uniquely valuable? And finally, we talk about Artemis III - what is the mission profile and what are the stakes for SpaceX and Blue Origin? articles.body: HBO and HBO Max's " Lanterns " served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were. While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
